#### April

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/COVID-19-Brazil-log.svg/500px-COVID-19-Brazil-log.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19-Brazil-log.svg)

Number of cases (blue) and number of deaths (red) on a [logarithmic scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithmic_scale "Logarithmic scale")

*   **6 April:** President Jair Bolsonaro threatened to fire the Minister of Health, [Luiz Henrique Mandetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Henrique_Mandetta "Luiz Henrique Mandetta"), after they clashed.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-45) Following criticism, Bolsonaro temporarily backed down.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-46)
*   **9 April:** The federal government sent out its first financial assistance ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese"): Auxílio emergencial) to the public. Over 2.5 million people received R$600 ($116).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-48)
*   **10 April:** Brazil confirmed the thousandth coronavirus-related death, as the number of confirmed cases neared 20,000.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-49)

The virus had reached remote locations; a [Yanomami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanomami "Yanomami") teen died of it in [Roraima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roraima "Roraima").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-50)
*   **14 April:** The Ministry of Health reported a total of 25,262 confirmed cases and 1,532 confirmed deaths. Over 14,000 people were declared recovered, although they were not confirmed virus-free, only discharged from a hospital or asymptomatic.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-51)
*   **16 April:** President Bolsonaro fired the Minister of Health, [Luiz Henrique Mandetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_Henrique_Mandetta "Luiz Henrique Mandetta"), over disagreements about [social distancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_distancing "Social distancing") guidelines.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-52) He said he would appoint a health minister who favored reopening businesses "as quickly as possible".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-53) Shortly afterwards, [Nelson Teich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Teich "Nelson Teich") was appointed to replace him.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-54)
*   **20 April:** Several cities started to ease social isolation guidelines in favor of [contact tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contact_tracing "Contact tracing"). Some retail stores were allowed to open as long as customers wore masks, the number of in-person customers was reduced, and customer personal information was tracked.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   **24 April:** Brazil confirmed more than fifty thousand cases.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-55)
*   **30 April:** Brazil overtook China's official number of confirmed cases, surpassing 87,000 [[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-56)

#### May

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/32/Comit%C3%AA_Covid-19_distribui_3_mil_m%C3%A1scaras_protetivas_em_Taguatinga_%2849916886416%29.jpg/250px-Comit%C3%AA_Covid-19_distribui_3_mil_m%C3%A1scaras_protetivas_em_Taguatinga_%2849916886416%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Comit%C3%AA_Covid-19_distribui_3_mil_m%C3%A1scaras_protetivas_em_Taguatinga_(49916886416).jpg)

Distribution of face masks in [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia "Brasília")

*   **3 May:** Brazil confirmed more than a hundred thousand cases; the number of cases had doubled in less than 10 days.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-57)
*   **7 May:** Several cities in the northern states of Amazonas and Pará begun issuing lockdown measures in order to curb the spread of the virus.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-58) Other cities in other states consider doing the same.
*   **9 May:** Brazil confirmed more than ten thousand deaths; the number of deaths had doubled in less than two weeks.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-59)
*   **c. 11 May:** Brazilian care centers initiate use of the [hug tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hug_tunnel "Hug tunnel") to allow elderly people to safely be in proximity to loved ones.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-60)
*   **14 May:** Brazil confirmed more than 200,000 cases; the number of cases had doubled in 11 days.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-61)

The state of Ceará became the state with the second most confirmed cases, overtaking Rio de Janeiro.
*   **15 May:** Brazil's minister of Health, [Nelson Teich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Teich "Nelson Teich"), resigned less than a month after being nominated. He cited reasons for this action similar to those of his predecessor: his clashes with the president over the use of [hydroxychloroquine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroxychloroquine "Hydroxychloroquine"), the social distancing guidelines, and being overruled on rules he was supposed to define.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-62)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-63) General [Eduardo Pazuello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Pazuello "Eduardo Pazuello") assumed the role of Interim Minister of Health, until an official replacement could be found.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-64)
*   **26 May:**[Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters "Reuters") reported that according to four officials, the Ministry of Health's initial 13 March response to the pandemic was halted and scaled back by President Bolsonaro less than a day later, with power transferred on 16 March from the ministry to the office of General [Walter Souza Braga Netto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Souza_Braga_Netto "Walter Souza Braga Netto"), the [Cabinet Chief of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Staff_of_the_Presidency_(Brazil) "Chief of Staff of the Presidency (Brazil)").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-65)
*   **31 May:** Brazil confirmed more than five hundred thousand cases; the number of cases had doubled in less than 14 days.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-66)

#### June

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Teste_r%C3%A1pido_de_covid-19_para_os_profissionais_da_sa%C3%BAde._%2850009226833%29.jpg/250px-Teste_r%C3%A1pido_de_covid-19_para_os_profissionais_da_sa%C3%BAde._%2850009226833%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Teste_r%C3%A1pido_de_covid-19_para_os_profissionais_da_sa%C3%BAde._(50009226833).jpg)

COVID-19 testing in São Paulo

*   **1 June:** Brazil confirmed more than 30,000 deaths.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-67)
*   **5 June:** The Brazilian government shut down its official website with COVID-19 daily reports, and stated it will no longer report the total number of deaths or active cases.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-68)
*   **6 June:**[Carlos Wizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Wizard_Martins "Carlos Wizard Martins"), the new Secretary of Science and Technology of the Ministry of Health, claimed that states are inflating the number of COVID-19 deaths in Brazil as a budget diversion scheme, and called for a recount of the total number of deaths.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-69)
*   **7 June:** The government decided that it will no longer publish cumulative COVID-19 numbers, claiming that former numbers may have been misleading. The health ministry plans to publish only the numbers of new cases and deaths in the past 24 hours.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-71) In response, large media groups in the country established a council to keep recording and publishing data according to the original method, amid claims that the government's initiative could be a maneuver to mislead the population instead.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-72)
*   **9 June:** A court order forced the Brazilian government to continue publishing cumulative case and death counts.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-74)

#### July

*   **6 July:** President Bolsonaro has a fever and was tested for coronavirus.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-75)
*   **7 July:** President Bolsonaro tests positive for COVID-19.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-76)
*   **25 July:** President Bolsonaro tests negative for COVID-19.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-77)
*   **30 July:**[First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_Brazil "First Lady of Brazil")[Michelle Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Bolsonaro "Michelle Bolsonaro") tests positive for COVID-19.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-78)

#### August

*   **3 August:** General Braga Netto, the chief of staff to President Bolsonaro, tests positive for COVID-19.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-79)
*   **8 August:** Brazil reaches three million infections and 100,000 deaths.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-80)
*   **25 August:** Senator [Flávio Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fl%C3%A1vio_Bolsonaro "Flávio Bolsonaro"), the eldest son of President Bolsonaro, tests positive for COVID-19.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-81)

#### September

*   **3 September:** Brazil reaches four million infections and about 125,000 deaths.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-82)
*   **9 September:** A two month old child dies of COVID-19 in [São Bernardo do Campo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Bernardo_do_Campo "São Bernardo do Campo"), possible the youngest death in the [ABC Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_Region "ABC Region").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-83)

#### October

*   **6 October:** Brazil reaches five million infections.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-84)

#### November

*   **20 November:** Brazil reaches six million infections.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-85)

#### December

*   **25 December:** Brazil reaches 190,000 deaths.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-86)
*   **31 December:** Variant [B117](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lineage_B.1.1.7 "Lineage B.1.1.7") is identified in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_(state) "COVID-19 pandemic in São Paulo (state)").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-87)

### 2021

#### January

See also: [Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine during the COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroquine_and_hydroxychloroquine_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine during the COVID-19 pandemic"), [Ivermectin §COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin#COVID-19 "Ivermectin"), and [COVID-19 pandemic in Amazonas (Brazilian state)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Amazonas_(Brazilian_state) "COVID-19 pandemic in Amazonas (Brazilian state)")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/COVID-19_vaccination_campaign_in_Brazil_%282021%29_H.jpg/250px-COVID-19_vaccination_campaign_in_Brazil_%282021%29_H.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19_vaccination_campaign_in_Brazil_(2021)_H.jpg)

The vaccination campaign begins.

*   **7 January:** Brazil reaches 200,000 deaths.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-88)
*   **11 January:** The [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)") pressures the administration of the city of [Manaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manaus "Manaus") to adopt [chloroquine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroquine "Chloroquine") and [ivermectin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivermectin "Ivermectin") as "premature treatment" drugs, stating that not using them would be "inadmissible".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-89) (The use of ivermectin as a supposed "miracle" drug for COVID-19 was already widespread as of December 2020[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil&action=edit) despite there being no good scientific evidence supporting such usage.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-90))
*   **12 January:** Researchers from the Brazil-UK CADDE Project announce the discovery of a variant of strain in Manaus, which was called P.1.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-91) According to Felipe Naveca, a scientist at the [Oswaldo Cruz Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswaldo_Cruz_Foundation "Oswaldo Cruz Foundation"), there is no doubt that the variant appeared in the Amazon, and may be more contagious. In the view of the researcher [Ester Sabino](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ester%20Sabino "pt:Ester Sabino"), from Institute of Tropical Medicine, the resurgence of cases in Manaus was associated with the novel P.1 SARS-CoV-2 variant,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-92) which was later labeled as Gamma variant of concern by World Health Organization.
*   **14 January:** Demand for oxygen peaked in the city of [Manaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manaus "Manaus"), in [Amazonas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazonas_(Brazilian_state) "Amazonas (Brazilian state)"), and the city could not supply the demand. Some patients died of asphyxiation,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-93) and some were transferred to other states. The city implemented an overnight curfew.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-95) Venezuelan Foreign Minister [Jorge Arreaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Arreaza "Jorge Arreaza"), on instructions from [Nicolás Maduro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Maduro "Nicolás Maduro"), offered his country's oxygen stock to the government of Amazonas.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-96) It was later revealed that Brazilian officials had been warned of the oxygen supply crisis six days earlier.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-97)
*   **17 January:**[Anvisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Health_Regulatory_Agency "Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency") has authorized the emergency use of [CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac") and the [AstraZeneca-Oxford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford%E2%80%93AstraZeneca_COVID-19_vaccine "Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine") vaccine.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-98) Monica Calazans, 54 years old and part of the risk group, a nurse in the fight against COVID, became the first Brazilian to take CoronaVac officially outside the tests.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-99)
*   **21 January:** Research from the [University of São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "University of São Paulo") and the [Conectas Direitos Humanos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conectas_Direitos_Humanos?action=edit&redlink=1 "Conectas Direitos Humanos (page does not exist)")[[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conectas%20Direitos%20Humanos "pt:Conectas Direitos Humanos")] revealed the "existence of an institutional strategy to spread the virus, promoted by the Brazilian Government under the leadership of the Presidency of the Republic".[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-101)

Pharmaceutical company União Quimica started production of [Sputnik V vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputnik_V_COVID-19_vaccine "Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine") in Brazil in January 2021.

*   **27 January:** Brazil reaches 220,000 deaths.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-102)_[The Lancet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lancet "The Lancet")_ publishes an article concerning the possible causes of an "unexpected" increase in January hospital admissions in Manaus, including the emergence of the [P.1. variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lineage_P.1 "Lineage P.1"). #### February

*   **1 February:** Since vaccination started on 17 January, 2,220,216 people have been vaccinated. This represents 1.05% of the national population, and 25.21% of the doses received by the states.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-105)
*   **9 February:** After repeatedly stating he did not approve of, and that his administration would not purchase Chinese company [Sinovac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech")'s vaccine, Bolsonaro backpedals and states that he was "never against the vaccine".[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-sinovac-lie-em-106) Bolsonaro also stated he did not intend to take the vaccine,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-sinovac-lie-em-106) and is the only [G20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G20 "G20") leader to have done so.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-107)
*   **16 February:** Brazil reaches 240,000 deaths.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-108)  
Since vaccination started on 17 January, 5,505,049 people have been vaccinated – of which 308,791 have also received the second dose. This represents 2.6% of the national population.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-109)
*   **17 February:**[Serrana, São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serrana,_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "Serrana, São Paulo") participates in a study wherein 100% of its adult population is vaccinated with [CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac") while other communities complain of shortages. Prior to the mass vaccination, 5% of Serrana's population had been infected, one of the highest rates in Brazil. Only two million doses of vaccines have arrived in the country so far.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-110)
*   **25 February:** On the day Brazil reached a record high 1,582 deaths by COVID-19 in 24 hours, during his weekly livestream, Bolsonaro questioned the efficacy of [mask usage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_masks_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic") and [lockdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns"), citing an unspecified German study to justify his doubts on the first.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-feb-26-mask-111) The study that seems to have been referenced by Bolsonaro[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-112) has been debunked multiple times, and is deemed non-scientific.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-113)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-114)

Additionally, they argue that Bolsonaro committed crimes against humanity for attempting to prevent efforts against the pandemic.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-129) The Brazilian Senate opened the [CPI da COVID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_CPI "COVID-19 CPI") that will also "investigate the use of federal funds passed to the federal entities to combat the new coronavirus."[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-130) On this same day, in [Itirapina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itirapina "Itirapina") (São Paulo), 46 people were mistakenly vaccinated with Coronavac, as opposed to the influenza vaccine.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-ErrorABC-131)
*   **14 April:** Five children, between 7 months and 4 years old, were mistakenly vaccinated with the [CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac") in [Diadema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diadema,_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "Diadema, São Paulo") instead of the Influenza vaccine. The children will be followed for 42 days, but there have been few studies yet on how this vaccine performs in children.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-ErrorABC-131) The BBC reported that the international non-governmental organization Vital Strategies estimates that about 2,000 children under age 9 (including 1,300 babies) have died in Brazil from COVID-19, although the Health Ministry's numbers reflect only about a third that number.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-133)

## Vaccination

Main article: [COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil "COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil")

The [COVID-19 vaccination campaign in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil "COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil") is an ongoing mass [immunization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunization "Immunization") campaign for the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil. It started on 17 January 2021, when the country had 210 thousand deaths.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_the_guardian-148)

The [Instituto Butantan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Butantan "Instituto Butantan") imported the first 6 million doses of [CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac") in a collaboration with the Chinese company [Sinovac Biotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_butantan-149)

There is no deadline forecast for immunizing the country's entire population due to the lack of supplies for vaccine production[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_g1_2021-01-18-150) and also due to political disputes between the São Paulo state government and the [Jair Bolsonaro government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Jair_Bolsonaro "Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro").[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_folha_painel-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_uol-152)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-COVID-19_vaccination_in_Brazil_jornal_nacional-153)

According to a June 2022 study published in _[The Lancet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lancet "The Lancet")_, COVID-19 vaccination in Brazil prevented an additional 1 million deaths from 8 December 2020 to 8 December 2021.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-154)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-155)

## Responses

### Scientific research and forecast

On 19 March 2020, scientists predicted up to 2 million deaths in Brazil in the worst-case scenario without measures to contain the virus. They pointed out that a policy of [social distancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_distancing "Social distancing") was one of the most effective measures given the lack of a [vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine "Vaccine").[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto10-156)

On 20 March, experts from Italy warned that the coronavirus growth curve in Brazil would repeat that of European countries. An observatory with physicists from [USP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "University of São Paulo"), [University of Campinas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Campinas "University of Campinas"), [São Paulo State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_State_University "São Paulo State University"), [University of Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bras%C3%ADlia "University of Brasília"), [Federal University of ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_University_of_ABC "Federal University of ABC"), [UC Berkeley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Berkeley "University of California, Berkeley") and the [University of Oldenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oldenburg "University of Oldenburg") showed that the number of infected people, considering data from 19 March, had been doubling every 54 hours, and that the case total would exceed 3,000 by the 24th.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto13-157)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-158)

On 21 March, researchers began to mobilize to increase the availability of testing in Brazil. The [Federal University of Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_University_of_Rio_de_Janeiro "Federal University of Rio de Janeiro") was attempting to create a [serology test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serology#Serological_tests "Serology"), as opposed to the more common [PCR test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction "Polymerase chain reaction"), to detect infections through a patient's blood samples.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto6-159) Minister of Health Luiz Henrique Mandetta said that the number of cases would increase exponentially until the end of June.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-exame-160)

On 23 March, a report from [FGV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funda%C3%A7%C3%A3o_Getulio_Vargas "Fundação Getulio Vargas") economist Emerson Marçal predicted a negative 2020 GDP of up to 4.4% due to the effect of the coronavirus.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-161)

Eleven COVID-19 patients died after receiving high doses of the anti-malarial drug [chloroquine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroquine "Chloroquine") in a study in Brazil. This was reported in mid-April. The study was halted.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-162)

On 15 August 2020, three joint-ventures began testing a new COVID-19 vaccine in Brazil. The origin of the research and development became a hugely debated issue, further complicated by conspiracy theories spread by anti-vax groups and renowned political allies of Jair Bolsonaro, Brazilian President along with xenophobia.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-163)

Brazilian firefighters assigned to aid in the detection of suspected cases

On 17 March, Brazilian authorities partially closed [their border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil%E2%80%93Venezuela_border "Brazil–Venezuela border") with Venezuela. Health Minister Luiz Henrique Mandetta had urged closure of the border due to Venezuela's [collapsing health system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortages_in_Venezuela "Shortages in Venezuela").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-165) The state of [Santa Catarina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Catarina_(state) "Santa Catarina (state)") declared a state of emergency, and ordered the closure of all non-essential businesses, and suspended public transit, inter-city and inter-state buses, public meetings, concerts, theatres, sporting events and religious services.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-166)

On 18 March, Rio de Janeiro and five other municipalities—[São Gonçalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Gon%C3%A7alo,_Rio_de_Janeiro "São Gonçalo, Rio de Janeiro"), [Guapimirim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guapimirim "Guapimirim"), [Niterói](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niter%C3%B3i "Niterói"), [Nova Iguaçu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nova_Igua%C3%A7u "Nova Iguaçu"), and [Mesquita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesquita,_Rio_de_Janeiro "Mesquita, Rio de Janeiro")—in the state of Rio de Janeiro had declared a state of emergency to help contain the coronavirus.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto-167)

The following day, the government of Rio Grande do Sul declared a public emergency situation. Among the measures adopted were the prohibition of interstate travel and the restriction of items purchased in the markets.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto1-168)

On 20 March, the government of Rio Grande do Norte declared a public emergency situation.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto12-169)

On 21 March, cases in São Paulo rose almost 40% in two hours. Deaths also increased in the period. The state issued a lockdown order for non-essential businesses, lasting from 24 March⁠ through at least ⁠7 April.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-170)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-171)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/F%C3%A1brica_do_DF_produz_vacina_Sputnik_V_%2850874843532%29.jpg/250px-F%C3%A1brica_do_DF_produz_vacina_Sputnik_V_%2850874843532%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:F%C3%A1brica_do_DF_produz_vacina_Sputnik_V_(50874843532).jpg)

Brazilian Governor [Ibaneis Rocha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibaneis_Rocha "Ibaneis Rocha") ([Federal District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_District_(Brazil) "Federal District (Brazil)"), in blue suit) wearing a face mask

Cities in the Campinas region declared an emergency situation. In addition to the metropolis, Hortolândia, Holambra, Indaiatuba, Itapira, Jaguariúna, Mogi Guaçu, Mogi Mirim, Paulínia, Sumaré and Águas de Lindoia issued decrees with special measures to contain the spread of COVID-19 cases. Valinhos and Vinhedo declared a state of public emergency.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-172)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-173)

On 9 May, the government of Rio Grande do Sul established a new social distancing plan. Given that some areas were more affected than others, the local government organized the state in 20 sectors. Each sector is ranked – according to the number of cases, hospital occupancy rates, and other factors – from Yellow (low risk), to Orange, Red, and Black (high risk). The goal of this scale is to be able to respond better to the current pandemic, and allow the population on lower risk areas to return to a somewhat normal life.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-174)

### Presidential responses

In a press briefing on 27 March 2020, Bolsonaro downplayed the possibility that COVID-19 could spread rapidly nationwide, arguing that Brazilians "never catch anything", and that there was a possibility that portions of the population were already immune.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:3-175) He has described the threat of COVID-19 as being exaggerated and as a media-created "fantasy".[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:1-176)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:3-175)[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-177)

#### Masks

On 15 March 2020, Bolsonaro made an appearance during a pro-government rally in [Brasília](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bras%C3%ADlia "Brasília"), interacting with his supporters. He faced criticism for participating without taking precautions (such as [wearing a mask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_masks_during_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic")), especially after his press secretary was infected following his presidential visit to the United States.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-178)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto11-179) On 27 November 2020, he reiterated his belief that masks are ineffective at limiting the spread of the virus, and he said that discussion of masks was "the last taboo to fall".[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:4-180)

#### Vaccines

Bolsonaro opposed proposals to purchase the [Sinovac Biotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech") vaccine, but the country's health agency granted approval for Phase 3 trials in São Paulo.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-181)

On 27 November 2020, Bolsonaro acknowledged that the country's health agency had approved effective vaccines, but added that he personally would not take any COVID-19 vaccine.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:4-180) In 2021, it was revealed that he had repeatedly refused offerings by [Pfizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer "Pfizer") to get tens of millions of doses of [their vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer%E2%80%93BioNTech_COVID-19_vaccine "Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine") at a discount.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-182) In contrast, millions of [Covaxin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covaxin "Covaxin") doses were purchased in June 2021 at elevated prices.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-183)

In October 2021, Facebook and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") removed a video in which Bolsonaro falsely claimed that COVID-19 vaccines could increase the risk of contracting [AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIDS "AIDS").[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-184) The original source of the claim was _[The Exposé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Expos%C3%A9 "The Exposé")_, a British [conspiracist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracist "Conspiracist") website.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:72-185)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:12-186) The [Brazilian Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Supreme_Court "Brazilian Supreme Court") ordered a probe to be opened into Bolsonaro for the claim.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-187)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-188)

#### Misinformation about treatments

In late March 2020, [Facebook, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook,_Inc. "Facebook, Inc.") and Twitter pulled social media posts by Bolsonaro that promoted [hydroxychloroquine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroxychloroquine "Hydroxychloroquine") as an effective treatment for COVID-19, with the companies considering them [misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation_related_to_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Misinformation related to the COVID-19 pandemic") that could cause physical harm, and a contradiction of authoritative health information respectively. Twitter also pulled a similar post by Bolsonaro that called for the reopening of the economy.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-189)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:7-14)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-190)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-191)

#### Concern about business interests

On 15 March 2020, Bolsonaro claimed that businesses were profiting off "hysteria", and he said the public should not react with "[neurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurosis "Neurosis")."[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:0-192)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto3-193)

He has opposed proposals to suspend interstate travel between states with cases,[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-194) and the closure of businesses (including malls and weekly outdoor markets), arguing in the case of the latter that they were "extreme measures" that would hurt the economy. Governor of [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_(state) "São Paulo (state)") João Doria criticised President Bolsonaro for his inaction on COVID-19, which had required individual states to take on responsibilities that should have been taken on at the federal level.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-195)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-196)

On 19 March, President Bolsonaro's son [Eduardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduardo_Bolsonaro "Eduardo Bolsonaro") shared a Twitter post that which blamed the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") for the worldwide spread of COVID-19. As China is Brazil's largest trading partner, the post provoked criticism from Chinese diplomats such as Yang Wanming – who argued that Bolsonaro family was "the great poison of this country."[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-197)

In a presidential address on 22 March 2020, Bolsonaro continued with these arguments,[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-198) criticising the use of "[scorched earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorched_earth "Scorched earth")" mitigation measures such as closing businesses and restricting travel, questioning the closure of schools due to there being more infections among the elderly, and accusing the media of spreading a "feeling of dread" among the population.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:5-199)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:6-200)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:2-201)

#### Comments by Bolsonaro

In a presidential address on 22 March 2020, he argued that the lives of Brazilians needed to return to normality, and that "because of my background as an athlete, I wouldn't need to worry if I was infected by the virus. I wouldn't feel anything or at the very worst it would be like a little flu or a bit of a cold."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:5-199)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:6-200)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:2-201)

In a televised interview on 23 March 2020, Bolsonaro criticised the protests against him, arguing that "the people will soon see that they were tricked by these governors and by the large part of the media when it comes to coronavirus".[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-202)

On 28 April 2020, when a reporter pointed out that Brazil's death toll had surpassed China's, he replied, "So what? I'm sorry, but what do you want me to do?"[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-203) In another interview in the same month, when questioned about the death toll in Brazil, Bolsonaro replied saying that "[He was] not a grave-digger."[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-204)

On 7 July 2020, after announcing that he had tested positive, Bolsonaro remarked "There's no reason for fear. That's life", and continued to criticise lockdown measures, arguing that "the majority of Brazilians contract this virus and don't notice a thing", and that "You can't just talk about the consequences of the virus that you have to worry about. Life goes on. Brazil needs to produce. You need to get the economy in gear."[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-205)[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-206)

In March 2021, when Brazil's death toll saw a record rise over a 24-hour period, Bolsonaro stated: "Stop whining. How long are you (the brazilian people) going to keep crying about it?"[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-207)

#### Political reactions and public opinion

On 21 March 2020, it was reported that Alcolumbre, president of the Chamber of Deputies Rodrigo Maia, and the leaders of the major parties in the [National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Congress_of_Brazil "National Congress of Brazil"), no longer believed that they could conduct productive dialogue on COVID-19 with Bolsonaro.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto9-208)

The 22 March 2020 presidential address was met with a negative response by many Brazilian politicians,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-210) as well as critics of Bolsonaro; in a Twitter post, journalist Ricardo Noblat referred to it as the "first political suicide broadcast live on national radio and television."[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:2-201) João Doria told CNN that Bolsonaro was "an unprepared and psychopathic leader."[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-211) The ongoing public protests against the President intensified during and after the address.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:2-201)[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-212)[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-213)

In mid-March 2020, [panelaços](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cacerolazo "Cacerolazo") began to occur in major cities such as Rio and São Paulo, including protests in support of the president, and others calling for his resignation.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-214) According to one poll, 64% of Brazilians rejected the way Bolsonaro had been handling the pandemic, while 44.8% supported his [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment "Impeachment"), an all-time high.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-215) According to some sources in Congress, Bolsonaro was shutting down political dialogue on purpose and forcing his impeachment to mobilize his supporters.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto9-208)

In October 2021, a Brazilian congressional panel voted to recommend criminally charging two companies and 78 individuals as laid out in a 1,288 report. Bolsonaro is one of the individuals described in the report; nine criminal charges were recommended for him, including "crimes against humanity."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:9-16)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-216)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-217)

[Natália Pasternak Taschner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nat%C3%A1lia_Pasternak_Taschner "Natália Pasternak Taschner"), the president of the [Instituto Questão de Ciência](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instituto_Quest%C3%A3o_de_Ci%C3%AAncia "Instituto Questão de Ciência"), [microbiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbiologist "Microbiologist"), and research scientist at the [University of São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "University of São Paulo"), has addressed the spread of misinformation from the government and other sources. She has appeared frequently on _[Jornal Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jornal\_Nacional "Jornal Nacional")_ and written a weekly science column for _[O Globo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O\_Globo "O Globo")_.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-218)

### Accountability of Federal Council of Medicine

Several scientific and health entities, such as the [Oswaldo Cruz Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oswaldo_Cruz_Foundation "Oswaldo Cruz Foundation"),[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-219) the [Brazilian Society for the Advancement of Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Society_for_the_Advancement_of_Science "Brazilian Society for the Advancement of Science"),[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-220) and the [National Health Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)"),[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-221) expressed concern and criticism of the [Federal Council of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Council_of_Medicine "Federal Council of Medicine")'s stances on the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil,[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-222) which is cited in [COVID-19 CPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_CPI "COVID-19 CPI").[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-223)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-224)

## Impact

### Economy

See also: [List of economic crises in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_economic_crises_in_Brazil "List of economic crises in Brazil")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/06/Entradasescgrussai.jpg/330px-Entradasescgrussai.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Entradasescgrussai.jpg)

A [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch_office "Branch office") of [SESC Hotels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servi%C3%A7o_Social_do_Com%C3%A9rcio "Serviço Social do Comércio") in [São João da Barra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Jo%C3%A3o_da_Barra "São João da Barra") had to close down due to the [financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_tourism "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism") caused by the pandemic.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-225)[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-226)[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-227)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-228)

Economists expect an [economic stagnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_stagnation "Economic stagnation") for the country in 2020.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-229) On 16 March, the [Ministry of Economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Economy_(Brazil) "Ministry of the Economy (Brazil)") announced a stimulus package of R$147.3 billion (US$29 billion) to help the economy against the effects of the pandemic.[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-230) The Brazilian government is also in negotiations with the [New Development Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Development_Bank "New Development Bank") to receive an aid package for its COVID-19 efforts; China received one billion USD from the same institution.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-231)

On 21 March, Economy Minister [Paulo Guedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Guedes "Paulo Guedes") announced a series of aid measures to reduce the impact on the economy. A scholarship for self-employed professionals, to the amount of R$200, is being prepared, in addition to the payment guarantee for workers who have reduced working hours.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-exame-160)

On 23 March, government announced package of R$85.8 billion for states and municipalities. The amount includes transfers to the health area, recomposition of transfers of constitutional funds and suspension of the maturity of debts of the states with the Union.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-232)

The economy shrunk by an unparalleled 9.7 percent in the second quarter of 2020 and plunged Brazil into a recession.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-233)

By the end of 2020, Brazil's GDP had shrunk by 4.1%; the worst recorded since 1990.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-234)

In 2020, Brazil was instrumental in the continued reduction of extreme [poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty "Poverty") in [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean"). This was largely due to the effective implementation of [fiscal policies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_policy "Fiscal policy") aimed at mitigating the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-235)

### Education

By 20 March, the pandemic had [impacted education all over the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_education "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education"). There were nationwide school closures in over 100 countries. However, President Jair Bolsonaro announced few country-wide measures to slow the spread of the virus,[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:17-236)[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:18-237) and because the federal government decided not to cancel classes in the whole country, lower levels of government have done so on independently. Municipal, state, and private schools and universities had different reactions regarding the suspension of classes. Classes were suspended at once, gradually or not at all. Some of them were replaced with [distance education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_education "Distance education") or simply postponed. Because of that, there are only "localized" (as opposed to "national") school closures, according to [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO").[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-UNESCO-238)

### Employment

From 2015 to 2016, Brazil experienced a crippling recession that saw its economy decrease by about 7% with an extremely small amount of growth seen from 2017 to 2018.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-239) At the beginning of the pandemic, Brazil had hitherto been suffering from this economic dilemma. With COVID-19 now added to the list of problems, 83.5% of Brazil's labour market were pushed into an exposed state.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-240) According to Rogério Barbosa, a professor at the IESP Institute for Social and Political Studies; due to the pandemic, between social-distancing and the fear of becoming infected by the virus, between 17 and 19 million people have stopped searching for employment in Brazil.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-241)

### Environment

Further information: [Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the environment §Deforestation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_the_environment#Deforestation "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the environment")

The [deforestation of the Amazon rainforest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deforestation_of_the_Amazon_rainforest "Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest") has accelerated during the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil, increasing by over half compared to baseline levels, according to satellite imagery.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-AmazonABC-11)[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-242) COVID-19 threatens [indigenous communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_in_Brazil "Indigenous peoples in Brazil") in the Amazon region.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-243)

### Favelas

Low socio-economic status is known to be a risk factor for COVID-19.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-244) By 17 March, residents of [favelas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Favelas "Favelas") in Rio de Janeiro suffered from a lack of water. Without water to clean themselves, this made them vulnerable to the proliferation of coronavirus. Water did not reach parts of the [Baixada Fluminense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baixada_Fluminense "Baixada Fluminense") and the North Zone of [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"). Among the affected areas are the Chatuba de [Mesquita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesquita,_Rio_de_Janeiro "Mesquita, Rio de Janeiro"), Camarista, [Méier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A9ier "Méier") and [Complexo do Alemão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complexo_do_Alem%C3%A3o "Complexo do Alemão") communities. The infectious disease doctor and pediatrician Cristiana Meirelles said that without clean running water, the situation of fighting the epidemic would become catastrophic.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-245)[Cufa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cufa "Cufa") (_Central Única das Favelas_, a NGO that operates with Favelas) called for measures to contain coronavirus in favelas. Government actions did not include the economically fragile, a contingent that totals more than 70 million people, said the organization.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-246)

Some areas of Maré had been without water for two days, and other areas were reported to have been without water for two weeks.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-247)[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-248)

### Healthcare

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Respiradores_da_USP_utilizados_do_Incor_%2850119127303%29.jpg/250px-Respiradores_da_USP_utilizados_do_Incor_%2850119127303%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Respiradores_da_USP_utilizados_do_Incor_(50119127303).jpg)

Doctors check on a patient on a [ventilator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventilator "Ventilator") at [InCor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_Institute,_University_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "Heart Institute, University of São Paulo") in São Paulo.

Following the first reported cases in Brazil, there were concerns whether its healthcare system would be able to deal with the pandemic. On 12 March, the Ministry of Health requested an additional R$10 billion (US$2.1 billion) to the federal budget as part of its efforts to manage the pandemic.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-249) It estimated that 2,000 intensive care units would be immediately needed.[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-250)

On 18 March 2020 hospitals in São Paulo denounced a lack of health materials, such as masks, gloves and hand sanitizer, caused by an increase in prices.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto8-251)[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto7-252) According to them, packages of masks went from R$4.50 in January to R$140 by 17 March. The government said it will negotiate with industry to meet the demand.[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-253)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-254)

In Salvador, local shops experienced shortages of masks and hand sanitizer.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto4-255) Rio and five other municipalities in the state declared an emergency to contain the coronavirus. The municipalities of São Gonçalo and Guapimirim also declared a state of emergency; Niterói, Nova Iguaçu and Mesquita declared an emergency situation in the area of public health.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto-167)

On 19 March 2020 scientists predicted up to 2 million deaths in Brazil in the worst-case scenario, without measures to contain the coronavirus. They pointed out that maintaining social distance was one of the most effective measures in the absence of a vaccine.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto10-156) Their conclusion came after analyzing the growth curve of COVID-19 cases in Brazil. The contagion rate was the same as that registered in Italy, as the number of infected people had been doubling every 54 hours. According to estimates, the number of confirmed cases might reach 3,000 by 24 March.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto13-157) According to the Ministry of Health, the number of infected patients would grow exponentially until the end of June.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-exame-160) The mayor of Belo Horizonte, Alexandre Kalil (PSD), asked General Altair José Polsin, commander of the 4th Army Region, for the temporary assignment of 51 professionals from the army garrison to assist in the demands of fighting the coronavirus. The Brazilian Army has not yet said whether it will meet this demand. Peak cases of COVID-19 in Belo Horizonte were expected to occur in the first week of April. In an interview, the health secretary announced the creation of two more Respiratory Disease centers and was studying placing PMs to serve the population.[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-256)[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto5-257)

The Government of Rio Grande do Sul decreed a public emergency situation, with measures including the prohibition of interstate travel and the restriction of items purchased in the markets, with the decree in force from 19 March 2020.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto1-168) Employees at four public hospitals in the city of São Paulo reported a shortage of materials such as alcohol gel, masks and gloves when caring for patients with suspected coronavirus. Professionals in the Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) reported a shortage of masks and rationing of gel alcohol, though the situation of public-service workers was different from that of private hospitals in São Paulo, the latter of which had sufficient equipment to care for patients.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto8-251)[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto7-252) Stores specializing in medical supplies no longer had alcohol gels and masks, including N95 masks used by health professionals. Street vendors were reported to be taking advantage of the demand for equipment and trying to profit from it.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto4-255)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Capacita%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_profissionais_da_Sa%C3%BAde_que_atuar%C3%A3o_nos_terminais_de_%C3%B4nibus_-_49667698972.jpg/250px-Capacita%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_profissionais_da_Sa%C3%BAde_que_atuar%C3%A3o_nos_terminais_de_%C3%B4nibus_-_49667698972.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Capacita%C3%A7%C3%A3o_dos_profissionais_da_Sa%C3%BAde_que_atuar%C3%A3o_nos_terminais_de_%C3%B4nibus_-_49667698972.jpg)

Health professionals clean up public transport to prevent spread of the virus.

On 20 March the press reported that Brazil was contradicting the recommendation of the World Health Organization by only testing patients in a severe condition. João Gabbardo, executive secretary at the Ministry of Health, said that the criteria adopted would not change, and people with serious cases would be tested for COVID-19.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto2-40) The following day, a group of scientists announced they were developing new COVID-19 tests in Brazil. They expect to elaborate a test which will work with a single drop of blood from the patient. They expected it to be ready during the current outbreak of COVID-19, and hoped to engage some of the main Brazilian universities in its development.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto6-159) Without protective items, health workers improvised caps as masks in hospitals. In addition to the first cases of coronavirus in Acre, health professionals in the state had to deal with the lack of personal protective equipment (PPE). Some agents improvised with caps as masks.[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-258)

On 31 March, the U.S. federal government donated two million doses hydroxychloroquine to Brazil, for prophylactic and therapeutic use.[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-259)[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-260)[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-261)

Health professionals in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ) complained about the lack of conditions to work with patients in COVID-19. Doctors said there were no N95 masks, with a more efficient filter, at Hospital Salgado Filho. Unions said there was a shortage of personal protective equipment in hospitals.[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-262)

### Religious services

[Dom Odilo Scherer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odilo_Scherer "Odilo Scherer"), [Archbishop of São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archdiocese_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "Archdiocese of São Paulo"), had initially defended the position that churches should not be closed, arguing that there should be more daily services to diffuse large gatherings. Later, he declared the suspension of celebrations with the people.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-igrejas-263)[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-264)[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-265) Bishop [Edir Macedo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edir_Macedo "Edir Macedo"), founder of the [Universal Church of the Kingdom of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Church_of_the_Kingdom_of_God "Universal Church of the Kingdom of God"), also declared that services should not be suspended, as well as [Silas Malafaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silas_Malafaia "Silas Malafaia"), leader of [Assembleia de Deus Vitória em Cristo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assembleias_de_Deus "Assembleias de Deus").[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-igrejas-263) Malafaia said he would only close his churches if mandated by a court order. Macedo caused greater controversy after he dismissed coronavirus as a creation of the media.[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-266)

### Television programming

Brazilian networks started airing prevention tips during their programming. [Globo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rede_Globo "Rede Globo"), [SBT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistema_Brasileiro_de_Televis%C3%A3o "Sistema Brasileiro de Televisão"), [RecordTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RecordTV "RecordTV"), [Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rede_Bandeirantes "Rede Bandeirantes"), and [RedeTV!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RedeTV! "RedeTV!") announced they would stop production of all of their _[telenovelas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telenovelas "Telenovelas")_, and would record their [talk shows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_shows "Talk shows") without a live audience, while expanding journalism in their programming.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-267)[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-268)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-269)

The **COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil** has resulted in 38,042,729[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-1) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 704,045[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-1) deaths. The virus was confirmed to have spread to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") on 25 February 2020,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-4) when a man from [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo") who had traveled to [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-5) tested positive for the virus. The disease had spread to every [federative unit of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_units_of_Brazil "Federative units of Brazil") by 21 March. On 19 June 2020, the country reported its one millionth case and nearly 49,000 reported deaths.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-7) One estimate of [under-reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under-reporting#Disease "Under-reporting") was 22.62% of total reported COVID-19 mortality in 2020.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-10)

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") triggered a variety of responses from federal, state and local governments, having an impact on politics, education, the environment,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-AmazonABC-11) and the economy. On 27 March 2020 Brazil announced a temporary ban on foreign air travelers[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-12) and most state governors have imposed quarantines to prevent the spread of the virus.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-13) President [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") perpetuated [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_misinformation "COVID-19 misinformation") surrounding COVID-19 treatments[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:7-14) and its origins,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:8-15) and was accused of downplaying effective mitigations and pursuing a strategy of [herd immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herd_immunity "Herd immunity").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:9-16) In October 2021, a congressional panel recommended criminal charges against the president for his handling of the pandemic, including [crimes against humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_against_humanity "Crimes against humanity").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-:9-16)

As of 05 August 2026, Brazil, with 38,042,729[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-1) confirmed cases and 704,045[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-1) deaths, has the third-highest number of confirmed cases and second-highest death toll from COVID-19 in the world, behind only [those of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States") and [of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India "COVID-19 pandemic in India").

## Timeline

Main article: [Timeline of the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "Timeline of the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil")

### 2019

#### November

*   **27 November:** Two raw [sewage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sewage "Sewage") samples collected independently on 27 November 2019 in [Santa Catarina, Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Catarina_(state) "Santa Catarina (state)"), will later detect SARS-CoV-2 (100,000 copies per litre), 66 days in advance of the first COVID-19 confirmed case in the Americas. Subsequent samplings are positive on 11 December 2019 and 20 February 2020. These samples can show that SARS-CoV-2 was circulating in Brazil at least as early as late November 2019.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-17) However, this is highly contested by the scientific consensus which shows that the virus emerged in early December 2019 in Wuhan, China. Thus, it is highly unlikely that it was circulating in Brazil before early 2020.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-18) Researchers from the Institute of Tropical Medicine and international colleagues showed in the scientific journal Science that the first sustained transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in Brazil occurred between late February and early March 2020.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-19)

### 2020

On 28 January 2020, Brazil's [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Brazil) "Ministry of Health (Brazil)") announced that a suspected case of COVID-19 was being investigated in [Belo Horizonte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belo_Horizonte "Belo Horizonte"), involving a student who had recently returned from [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), China.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-21) Ministry also announced that they was investigating two other suspected cases in [Porto Alegre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porto_Alegre "Porto Alegre") and [Curitiba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curitiba "Curitiba").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-22)

On 3 February, it was announced that the Brazilian government would assist in helping citizens in Wuhan return to the country;[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-23) on 5 February, two planes were sent to Wuhan to [repatriate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repatriation "Repatriation") 34 citizens. The citizens and all other crew were to be quarantined and monitored for 18 days at a [Brazilian Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Air_Force "Brazilian Air Force") base in [Anápolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An%C3%A1polis "Anápolis").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-25) They were released ahead of schedule on 23 February, after repeatedly testing negative.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-26)

On 25 February, the first confirmed COVID-19 case in Brazil (and the first in South America) was announced by the Health Department of São Paulo – a 61-year-old man who had returned from [Lombardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombardy "Lombardy"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Italy "COVID-19 pandemic in Italy").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-28) A second case was confirmed soon after in another person who had recently returned from Italy.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-29) On 28 February, scientists of the [University of São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_S%C3%A3o_Paulo "University of São Paulo")'s Tropical Medicine Institute and the Adolfo Lutz Institute reported that they had [sequenced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequencing "Sequencing") the [genomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome "Genome") of these two cases, which had been separately introduced from [Northern Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Italy "Northern Italy") to Brazil on two occasions.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-31) In an address on 6 March, President [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") advised residents to "strictly follow the experts' recommendations as the best protective measure", but that "there is no reason to panic".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-32)

On 12 March, it was reported that Bolsonaro's press secretary [Fábio Wajngarten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A1bio_Wajngarten?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fábio Wajngarten (page does not exist)") had tested positive for COVID-19, prompting increased monitoring of Bolsonaro (who tested negative the next day)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-34) and his [cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Brazil "Cabinet of Brazil"). Wajngarten had also interacted with U.S. President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") and Vice President [Mike Pence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Pence "Mike Pence") during Bolsonaro's visit to Miami, [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Florida "COVID-19 pandemic in Florida") on 7 March.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-35) The number of cases within the cabinet began to increase, including Minister of Mines and Energy [Bento Albuquerque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bento_Albuquerque?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bento Albuquerque (page does not exist)"), and President of the Federal Senate [Davi Alcolumbre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davi_Alcolumbre "Davi Alcolumbre"); by 20 March, Brazil had the second-largest number of cases among members of a federal cabinet, overtaking Iran and behind only France.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-36)

On 13 March, the cruise ship _[Silver Shadow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver\_Shadow\_(ship) "Silver Shadow (ship)")_ arrived from [the Bahamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas") and docked in [Recife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recife "Recife"), Pernambuco, bearing 318 passengers and 291 crew members, including one suspected case of COVID-19. The ship was isolated by health authorities.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-37) On 17 March, Brazil recorded its first death.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-first_death-38) At this time, there were 291 confirmed cases in the country.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-39) By 20 March, state health departments reported almost 1,000 confirmed cases across 23 of 26 states and also in the Federal District.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-auto2-40) By 21 March, all Brazilian states had reported at least one confirmed case of COVID-19, with the most recent being Roraima.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-41) In the month since Brazil's first confirmed case, Brazil had 2,915 confirmed cases and 77 deaths.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-42)

On 28 March, the Ministry of Health reported that Brazil had 3,904 confirmed cases and 114 deaths, suggesting a mortality rate of 2.9%. Approximately 90% of deaths were people over 60 years of age, and most were men. In 84% of deaths, patients had at least one risk factor, most commonly heart disease, followed by diabetes and [pneumopathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonology "Pulmonology").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil#cite_note-44)
